body.statement: For any admissible interval band and any finite parameter set \(F\subset\mathcal U\), let \(A_F\) be the random subset of points in \(F\) whose entire curves are covered. Then \(c(A_F)=\max_{u,u'\in A_F}d_\Psi(u,u')\) is no larger than the band's maximum width, and each grid-point coverage probability is preserved. Conversely, every measurable rule selecting a subset \(A\subseteq F\) induces the pointwise envelope band of those selected curves, with maximum width exactly \(c(A)\), and padding this envelope by the uniform \(u\)-modulus transports coverage from a finite net to \(\mathcal U\). For each pair \((u,u')\), \(d_\Psi(u,u')\) is the maximum of finitely many second-order-cone programs obtained by intersecting the two critical-cone cell systems with \(\mathcal D\). These finite-set reductions apply to every randomized measurable interval-section band and do not impose a nonrandom-shape restriction.
body.justification: This reduction replaces an infinite-dimensional band action by a confidence-set decision under a computable geometry-specific diameter loss.
body.gap: FreybergerRai2018UniformBands, Definition 1, restricts bands to those induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands. Its Section 2.3 leads with weighted area; Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, while the paper supplies low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation specifically for weighted area. The separate unresolved target here is the externally randomized max-curve-diameter decision problem over all measurable interval-section bands. EvansHansenStark2005MinimaxConfidence instead uses additive set measure rather than curve diameter.
body.consumer: A numerical solver can compute exact pairwise curve distances with primal and dual conic certificates.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a finite set \(F\subset\mathcal U\) and a realization of an admissible band \(C\).  Write
\[
 \mathcal A_F(C)=\bigl\{u\in F:\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)\in C(t)
                    \text{ for every }t\in\mathcal D\bigr\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal L(C)=\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\operatorname{diam}C(t).
\]
The events in this finite definition are measurable by the simultaneous-coverage requirement in Definition \(\mathrm{def:local\mbox{-}band\mbox{-}class}\).  If \(u,u'\in\mathcal A_F(C)\), then both \(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)\) and \(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u',t)\) belong to the interval \(C(t)\) for every \(t\).  Hence
\[
 |\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)-\Psi_{\theta_0}(u',t)|
 \leq \operatorname{diam}C(t),
 \qquad
 d_\Psi(u,u')\leq\mathcal L(C).
\]
Taking the maximum over the finite accepted set proves
\[
 c\bigl(\mathcal A_F(C)\bigr)\leq\mathcal L(C).
\]
Moreover, for each \(u\in F\), the event \(u\in\mathcal A_F(C)\) is exactly the event that the entire curve indexed by \(u\) is covered.  Thus passing from the band to its accepted subset preserves every pointwise-in-parameter simultaneous-coverage probability.

Conversely, let a possibly randomized measurable rule select a subset \(A\subseteq F\).  For \(A\neq\varnothing\), define
\[
 C_A(t)=
 \left[\min_{u\in A}\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t),
       \max_{u\in A}\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)\right].
\]
The endpoints are measurable because they are extrema over a finite set.  Every selected curve is covered, and finiteness of \(A\) permits interchange of the two maxima:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\operatorname{diam}C_A(t)
 &=\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\max_{u,u'\in A}
      |\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)-\Psi_{\theta_0}(u',t)|\\
 &=\max_{u,u'\in A}\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}
      |\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)-\Psi_{\theta_0}(u',t)|
 =c_A.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(A=\varnothing\), take any fixed singleton interval; its diameter and the stipulated value \(c_A\) are both zero.  Randomization is retained as part of the subset rule, so this construction does not restrict the shape or randomization of the original class.

Now suppose that \(F\) is a \(\delta\)-net and that
\[
 \sup_{t\in\mathcal D}|\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)-
       \Psi_{\theta_0}(u_i,t)|\leq K_u\delta
\]
whenever \(u_i\in F\) is a nearest net point to \(u\).  Pad every nonempty envelope by \(K_u\delta\) at both endpoints.  If \(u_i\) is selected, the displayed inequality shows that the padded band covers the entire curve indexed by \(u\).  Its maximum width is at most \(c_A+2K_u\delta\).  This is the asserted deterministic transport from a net to \(\mathcal U\); the probability loss caused by replacing the law at \(u_i\) by the law at \(u\) is handled separately by total variation in the theorem.

It remains to establish computability of \(d_\Psi\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:local\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}map}\) states that \(\Psi_{\theta_0}\) is continuous and affine on each of finitely many polyhedral critical-cone cells.  Fix \(u,u'\).  For every pair of cells that can respectively contain \((u,t)\) and \((u',t)\), their intersection with the query restrictions has the form
\[
 \mathcal T_{ab}=\left\{t:A_{ab}t\leq b_{ab},\ 
 \mathbf 1^{\prime}t=0,\ t_k\geq0\text{ if }(v_0)_k=0,\
 \lVert t\rVert_2\leq L_0\right\}.
\]
On this set the curve difference is affine, say
\(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)-\Psi_{\theta_0}(u',t)=\beta_{ab}+\gamma_{ab}^{\prime}t\).  Therefore its absolute maximum on \(\mathcal T_{ab}\) is the larger of the two second-order-cone program values
\[
 \max_{t}\ \sigma(\beta_{ab}+\gamma_{ab}^{\prime}t)
 \quad\text{subject to }t\in\mathcal T_{ab},
 \qquad \sigma\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
The feasible set is compact, so each maximum is attained.  Taking the maximum over the finitely many nonempty cell pairs and the two signs gives exactly \(d_\Psi(u,u')\).  On shared boundaries the affine formulas agree because the strongly convex critical-cone quadratic program has a unique minimizer; hence using closed cell systems neither omits nor changes a boundary value.  This proves all assertions.
